newsitem.title: USA: Hexcel gets new contract with union.
newsitem.headline: Hexcel gets new contract with union.

text.p: Hexcel Corp said on Monday that it has reached agreement on a new long term contract with the Oil, Chemical and Atomic Workers International Union that represents the production and maintenance employees at Hexcel's Salt Lake City facility.
This contract ends a strike which began on November 2, 1996.
Hexcel also said that its board of directors has approved a project which will expand carbon fiber capacity and enhance product quality at the Salt Lake City plant.

The multi-million dollar project is response the growing worldwide demand for high quality aerospace carbon fibers and will increase Hexcel's carbon fiber capacity by up to 1.5 million pounds, the company said. Expansion should be completed by August 1997.
Hexcel said that some of the striking employees will begin to return to work Monday and the rest will be placed on a preferential hiring list.
According to the company, the agreement contains the same compensation and benefits package that was offered to, and rejected by, the union in December 1996.
All replacement workers will be retained by the company.
